headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Claude Code can write/modify the shared repo while spring-integration-samples is unverified and may be treated as a companion workflow, creating unsafe shared-state assumptions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read/write repo files and use MCP, while spring-integration-samples exposes no runtime surfaces and is not runnable. A prompt-injection bridge is therefore not documented and would require unusual manual copy-paste or file handoff, with small blast radius limited to text artifacts.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies untrusted text from files produced by agent_b into agent_a prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF agent_b is wrapped in a file-based workflow that agent_a parses as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep agent_b outputs out of agent_a prompts unless reviewed.
Use a plain-text quarantine folder for any handoff files.
Strip instruction-like text before pasting into agent_a.
Disable MCP servers not needed for the task.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all handoff files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd; spring-integration-samples has no declared data classes or network egress. There is no documented shared workspace or sensitive-data flow from agent_b, so leakage is limited to local file exposure if the operator co-locates data.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the same cwd used by agent_a, those files may be read.
IF agent_b is extended to process private documents in the same workspace, leakage risk rises.
mitigations: Use a dedicated empty workspace for agent_a.
Do not place secrets in the shared repo tree.
Review git status before each run.
Separate private documents from code directories.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation with OS permissions.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; spring-integration-samples is open-source but unverified and may be used as a companion workflow around the same repo. Shared mutable state via filesystem/git is explicitly present for agent_a, so concurrent edits can conflict even though agent_b has no declared write surface.
conditions: IF agent_b is run against the same repository or working tree, concurrent edits can collide.
IF both agents modify git state without locking, merge conflicts or lost updates can occur.
mitigations: Serialize edits to the repo.
Run git status before and after each agent turn.
Assign one agent as read-only reviewer.
Use separate branches per agent.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or task-queue coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code and modify git state, while spring-integration-samples is a sample repository that may be used as downstream material. If agent_b consumes agent_a's outputs without verification, mistakes can cascade into incorrect code or workflow steps; the interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF agent_b treats agent_a's generated files or summaries as authoritative, errors can propagate.
IF agent_a writes code or config that agent_b later executes or republishes, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Require human review of agent_a outputs before reuse.
Add a verification step in agent_b's workflow.
Compare generated artifacts against expected templates.
Keep agent_b read-only unless necessary.
requires-engineering: add automated tests or schema validation.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and can access local files, while spring-integration-samples declares no regulated data classes or residency constraints. No specific compliance mismatch is documented, so only a low-risk policy gap exists if private or regulated data is introduced into the shared workspace.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the workspace used by agent_a, policy review is required.
IF agent_b is repurposed to process personal or regulated data, residency/retention checks become necessary.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared repo.
Confirm retention settings before use.
Document which data classes each agent may touch.
Use separate storage for secrets.
requires-engineering: add a compliance gate for regulated inputs.
